title: DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize a measurable real-valued objective f over a closed convex set C. The objective is convex on C and may be nonsmooth. The public point x₀ belongs to C, and some constrained minimizer x⋆ satisfies ‖x₀−x⋆‖ ≤ R. The instance supplies f and C privately.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, spec.Instance and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, Instance and spec.admissible.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A subgradient query at x returns g(x,ξ). For every x in C, its mean s(x) satisfies f(y) ≥ f(x) + ⟨s(x),y−x⟩ for all y in C. The oracle uses independent sample coordinates with a common hidden law. The reply reveals the vector alone.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, spec.admissible and spec.Reply. LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, Query.subgradient and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: A projection query at any z returns the exact Euclidean projection onto C. Projection and stochastic subgradient queries each consume one call from the same fixed budget. The target setup allows unrestricted algorithms.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, Query.projection and the projection variational inequality in spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, spec. LongTails/Template.lean, Setup.numOracles, Setup.allowedAlgorithm and executeWithTrace.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x in C, the uncentered second moment satisfies E‖g(x,ξ)‖² ≤ G² + B²‖x−x₀‖². This permits heavy tails and allows both the mean subgradient norm and the noise scale to grow with distance from x₀. The public bounds B and G may each be zero.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, final moment condition in spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, spec.publicInput and spec.valid.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is Euclidean ℝᵈ. The algorithm knows d, x₀, B, G, δ, R and ε. The radius R > 0 bounds the initial distance to a minimizer and places no diameter bound on C.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, Vector, Public and the minimizer condition in spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, Public, spec.publicInput and spec.valid.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns a measurable vector X. The accuracy event is f(X)−f(x⋆) ≤ ε for a constrained minimizer x⋆ and public ε > 0. Any algorithm output meeting this criterion is permitted, including an average of feasible iterates.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, spec.Output, spec.successful and spec.valid. LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/Template.lean, Setup.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: X must belong to C for every seed realization, including realizations on which the objective gap exceeds ε.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, the universal feasibility clause in spec.successful.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: The probability of f(X)−f(x⋆) > ε is at most the public δ, where 0 < δ < 1. Probability is taken over the product of the algorithm seed law and the oracle sample-sequence law.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistanceGrowingSubgradient.lean, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/Setups/TerminalClippingConvex.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/Template.lean, Convergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The stochastic subgradient’s second-moment bound grows quadratically with distance from the public starting point on a potentially unbounded feasible set. The algorithm has a radius bound to a solution and pays for each projection onto the original feasible set.

descriptionHtml:
Convex Minimization with Distance-Dependent Subgradient Moments

We minimize a real-valued function f that is convex on a closed convex set C in d-dimensional Euclidean space. A given x0∈C lies within distance R>0 of a minimizer x⋆ on C. The oracle returns either an exact projection onto C or a random vector drawn using a fresh independent sample. At each x∈C, this vector has a subgradient mean relative to C and second moment at most B2∥x−x0∥2+G2, where B,G≥0. For ε>0 and 0<δ<1, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈C satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε with probability at least 1−δ.

The optimization problem is minx∈Cf(x). The algorithm receives the dimension d∈{0,1,2,…}, the starting point x0, and the parameters B,G,R,ε,δ. Both query types accept any point in Rd and share a single call budget.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and initial distance). The function f:Rd→R is Borel measurable. On the closed convex set C⊆Rd, it satisfies f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y) for every x,y∈C and t∈[0,1]. The point x0 belongs to C, and there exists x⋆∈argminx∈Cf(x) such that ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 2 (Subgradient mean and second moment). Let (ξk)k≥0 be independent measurable samples with common law ν on a measurable space Ω, independent of the algorithm’s randomness. A subgradient query at x on call k returns g(x,ξk), where g:Rd×Ω→Rd is jointly measurable. For each x∈C and ξ∼ν, the vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable and ∥g(x,ξ)∥2 is integrable. Writing m(x)=Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)], we require f(y)≥f(x)+⟨m(x),y−x⟩(y∈C),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)∥2]≤B2∥x−x0∥2+G2.

A projection query at z∈Rd returns the Euclidean projection ΠC(z). This map is measurable, takes values in C, and satisfies ⟨z−ΠC(z),u−ΠC(z)⟩≤0(u∈C). After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and belong to C for every realization. Under the joint law P of the samples and the algorithm’s randomness, it must satisfy P(f(x¯)−f(x⋆)>ε)≤δ.

theorems.referencesHtml:
• Yair Carmon and Oliver Hinder. The Price of Adaptivity in Stochastic Convex Optimization. 2024 (COLT, full proof in arXiv v1). Complexity: O(R2MR2log⁡(2/δ)/ε2) total oracle calls for averaged clipped SGD when 0<ε<GR, with one stochastic subgradient and one projection onto KR=domain∩B―(x0,R) per step. Here MR=G2+B2R2 bounds the root second moment at every query in KR.
  • Daniela Angela Parletta, Andrea Paudice, Massimiliano Pontil, and Saverio Salzo. High Probability Bounds for Stochastic Subgradient Schemes with Heavy Tailed Noise. 2024 (journal version, first preprint 2022). Complexity: O(R2MR2log⁡(2/δ)/ε2) total oracle calls for the averaged clipped projected subgradient method on KR when 0<ε<GR, with one stochastic subgradient and one projection onto KR per step. The diameter is at most 2R, and MR bounds both the Lipschitz constant on KR and the oracle standard deviation there.

comparisonHtml:
Let X⊆Rd be closed and convex, f measurable and convex on X, and x0,x⋆∈X with x⋆ minimizing f on X and ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. Each call returns an exact projection onto X or a jointly measurable sample g(x,ξ) with fresh IID noise. On X, Eg(x,ξ)∈∂Xf(x) and E∥g(x,ξ)∥2≤G2+B2∥x−x0∥2. Given x0, B,G≥0, R,ε>0, and 0<δ<1, return a feasible x^ with Pr{f(x^)−f(x⋆)>ε}≤δ.

Sufficient oracle budgets for convex minimization with distance-growing subgradient moments.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) DistanceGrowingSubgradientUpperBound (Ours) (review) 0 if GR≤ε, otherwise O(R2(G2+B2R2)ℓ/ε2)
(2) Derived bound (Parletta et al. 2024, Thm. 2(iii), Cor. 1) O(R2(G2+B2R2)ℓ/ε2) (1) formalizes the matched rate. On K, the second moment is at most v. Use confidence parameter min{δ,2/e} in (2).
(3) Derived bound (Liu and Zhou 2023, Thm. 3) O(R2vℓ2/ε2) (1) reduces ℓ2 to ℓ against (3) localized to K with known horizon and variance bound v.
(4) Derived bound (Alacaoglu et al. 2026, Cor. 3.4) O(R2v/(ε2δ2)) by Markov’s inequality, tuning with max{B,G/R} (1) gives a direct high-probability guarantee. The confidence factor drops from δ−2 for the expected-gap conversion in (4) to ℓ. (1) uses R for the ball projection. When BR≥G, the updates in (4) need only B.
(5) Last-iterate clipping (LongTails 2026) O(1+(BR2+G2/B)2ℓ2ε2), B,G>0 (1) saves a factor ℓ for the shared objective-gap target and allows B=0 or G=0. For 0<BR≪G, O(R2G2ℓ/ε2) replaces O(G4ℓ2/(B2ε2)). (1) guarantees accuracy for a uniform average. (5) guarantees it for the last iterate.

Abbr: v=G2+B2R2, ℓ=1+log⁡(1/δ), K=X∩{x:∥x−x0∥≤R}. Cost counts sampled subgradients and projections onto X. Rate comparisons use GR>ε.

import LongTails.Setups.TerminalClippingConvex

open MeasureTheory OracleTemplate

namespace LongTails.Setups.DistanceGrowingSubgradient

abbrev Public := TerminalClippingConvex.Public

def withSamples (p : Public) (Ω : Type) [MeasurableSpace Ω] : TerminalClippingConvex.Params :=
  { p with Ω := Ω }

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Public
  Public := Public
  Instance := TerminalClippingConvex.Instance
  Query := TerminalClippingConvex.Query
  Reply p := TerminalClippingConvex.Vector p.d
  Output p := TerminalClippingConvex.Vector p.d
  publicInput := id
  valid p := 0 ≤ p.B ∧ 0 ≤ p.G ∧ 0 < p.δ ∧ p.δ < 1 ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p I O := ∃ (Ω : Type) (m : MeasurableSpace Ω),
    TerminalClippingConvex.spec.admissible (@withSamples p Ω m) I O
  successful p := TerminalClippingConvex.spec.successful (withSamples p Unit)

end LongTails.Setups.DistanceGrowingSubgradient
